I will keep the farm simple and manageable this year. I am 73, my household has only two people, and I have just 5.5 mu, so I will not spread myself too thin. Since my system is mainly stevia and I have well irrigation, I will put more land into stevia and keep a smaller cotton area. I will use improved seed rather than anything risky or expensive, because I want steady establishment and more uniform growth. I will fertilize moderately, not heavily, because with a small farm I care more about stable returns and avoiding waste than chasing the highest possible yield. I will irrigate according to each crop’s need, with stevia getting more water because it responds better to moisture, while cotton will get fewer irrigations. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on a small plot and gives a clean seedbed without the heavier work of deep ploughing. I will keep pesticide sprays limited but timely, because I want to protect the crop without overspending or making field work harder than necessary. My aim this year is not maximum expansion; it is steady production, manageable labor, and dependable output from both crops.
